trajectory_messages.content:
I'm seeing a bug in the chat widget's message submission logic.

*   When a session is configured with both a permission profile and the external sandbox policy variant, and the user submits a message, the resulting user turn operation must include the permission profile that was set in the session configuration — it must not be dropped or replaced with a null value.

*   The permission profile must be preserved in the submitted user turn regardless of which sandbox policy variant is active, including the legacy external sandbox variant.


**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.
I'll investigate the chat widget's message submission logic to find where the permission profile is being dropped.

{"type": "text", "text": "I have all the information needed. Here is my report.

## Summary

The chat widget's message-submission logic lives in `/workspace/repo/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget.rs`. On submit, it decides whether to include the permission profile based on the sandbox policy variant, then constructs an `Op::UserTurn` via a helper in `app_command.rs`.

## 1. Where the user turn operation is constructed on submission

File: `/workspace/repo/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget.rs`

The construction happens inside `fn submit_user_message_with_history_and_shell_escape_policy` (defined at line 6179). The relevant block:

```rust
6413        let permission_profile = if matches!(
6414            self.config.permissions.sandbox_policy.get(),
6415            SandboxPolicy::ExternalSandbox { .. }
6416        ) {
6417            None
6418        } else {
6419            Some(self.config.permissions.permission_profile())
6420        };
6421        let op = AppCommand::user_turn(
6422            items,
6423            self.config.cwd.to_path_buf(),
6424            self.config.permissions.approval_policy.value(),
6425            self.config.permissions.sandbox_policy.get().clone(),
6426            permission_profile,
6427            effective_mode.model().to_string(),
6428            effective_mode.reasoning_effort(),
6429            /*summary*/ None,
6430            service_tier,
6431            /*final_output_json_schema*/ None,
6432            collaboration_mode,
6433            personality,
6434        );
```

The `AppCommand::user_turn` helper that wraps this into `Op::UserTurn` is at `/workspace/repo/codex-rs/tui/src/app_command.rs:140-170`:

```rust
140    pub(crate) fn user_turn(
141        items: Vec<UserInput>,
142        cwd: PathBuf,
143        approval_policy: AskForApproval,
144        sandbox_policy: SandboxPolicy,
145        permission_profile: Option<PermissionProfile>,
...
154        Self(Op::UserTurn {
155            items,
156            environments: None,
157            cwd,
158            approval_policy,
159            approvals_reviewer: None,
160            sandbox_policy,
161            permission_profile,
...
```

## 2. How the permission profile is passed / dropped relative to the sandbox policy variant

This is the key behavior (lines 6413-6420 above):

- If `self.config.permissions.sandbox_policy.get()` is `SandboxPolicy::ExternalSandbox { .. }`, the permission profile is **nulled to `None`**.
- Otherwise, it is set to `Some(self.config.permissions.permission_profile())`.

So when the session is running under the "external sandbox" (the legacy `SandboxPolicy::ExternalSandbox` variant), the permission profile is deliberately dropped and only the raw `sandbox_policy` is sent on the user turn. `permission_profile` is a plain accessor on `self.config.permissions` returning a `PermissionProfile`.

## 3. Sandbox policy variant definitions (including the external one)

File: `/workspace/repo/codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs`, `enum SandboxPolicy` at lines 1030-1081:

```rust
1030 #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Display, JsonSchema, TS)]
1031 #[strum(serialize_all = "kebab-case")]
1032 #[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "kebab-case")]
1033 pub enum SandboxPolicy {
1034     /// No restrictions whatsoever. Use with caution.
1035     #[serde(rename = "danger-full-access")]
1036     DangerFullAccess,
1037
1038     #[serde(rename = "read-only")]
1039     ReadOnly { network_access: bool },
1040
1047     /// Indicates the process is already in an external sandbox. Allows full
1048     /// disk access while honoring the provided network setting.
1049     #[serde(rename = "external-sandbox")]
1050     ExternalSandbox {
1052         #[serde(default)]
1053         network_access: NetworkAccess,
1054     },
1058     #[serde(rename = "workspace-write")]
1059     WorkspaceWrite {
1060         writable_roots: Vec<AbsolutePathBuf>,
1067         network_access: bool,
1073         exclude_tmpdir_env_var: bool,
1078         exclude_slash_tmp: bool,
1080     },
1081 }
```

There are four variants: `DangerFullAccess`, `ReadOnly`, `ExternalSandbox`, and `WorkspaceWrite`. Note: there is **no separate enum variant literally named "LegacyExternal"**. The "legacy external sandbox" terminology in the codebase refers to this `SandboxPolicy::ExternalSandbox` variant being a legacy representation, which is mapped to the newer `PermissionProfile::External` via `from_legacy_sandbox_policy` (see below).

`NetworkAccess` (used by `ExternalSandbox`) is at lines 1011-1021 (`Restricted` default, `Enabled`).

## 4. Permission profile enum + external/legacy mapping

File: `/workspace/repo/codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs`, `enum PermissionProfile` at lines 356-374:

```rust
356 /// Canonical active runtime permissions for a conversation, turn, or command.
357 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize, JsonSchema, TS)]
358 #[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")]
360 pub enum PermissionProfile {
361     /// Codex owns sandbox construction for this profile.
364     Managed {
365         file_system: ManagedFileSystemPermissions,
366         network: NetworkSandboxPolicy,
367     },
368     /// Do not apply an outer sandbox.
369     Disabled,
370     /// Filesystem isolation is enforced by an external caller.
373     External { network: NetworkSandboxPolicy },
374 }
```

The legacy → new mapping is `PermissionProfile::from_legacy_sandbox_policy` (`models.rs:499`), which relies on `SandboxEnforcement::from_legacy_sandbox_policy` (`models.rs:298-304`):

```rust
298    pub fn from_legacy_sandbox_policy(sandbox_policy: &SandboxPolicy) -> Self {
299        match sandbox_policy {
300            SandboxPolicy::DangerFullAccess => Self::Disabled,
301            SandboxPolicy::ExternalSandbox { .. } => Self::External,
302            SandboxPolicy::ReadOnly { .. } | SandboxPolicy::WorkspaceWrite { .. } => Self::Managed,
303        }
304    }
```

So legacy `SandboxPolicy::ExternalSandbox` maps to `SandboxEnforcement::External` → `PermissionProfile::External { network }`.

## 5. Session-config source of the permission profile

The `permission_profile` and `sandbox_policy` come from session configuration. Handling of the `SessionConfiguredEvent` in the chat widget is at `/workspace/repo/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget.rs:2368-2388`:

```rust
2368        let permission_sync = match event.permission_profile.clone() {
2369            Some(permission_profile) => self
...
2372                .set_permission_profile(permission_profile, event.cwd.as_path()),
...
2376                .set_legacy_sandbox_policy(event.sandbox_policy.clone(), event.cwd.as_path()),
...
2380            self.config.permissions.sandbox_policy =
2381                Constrained::allow_only(event.sandbox_policy.clone());
2382            let permission_profile = event.permission_profile.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| {
2383                codex_protocol::models::PermissionProfile::from_legacy_sandbox_policy(
2384                    &event.sandbox_policy,
2385                )
2386            });
2387            self.config.permissions.permission_profile =
2388                Constrained::allow_only(permission_profile);
```

This shows the session config carries both an optional `permission_profile` and a legacy `sandbox_policy`; when the profile is absent it is derived from the legacy sandbox policy.

The load-bearing logic for the described concern is `chatwidget.rs:6413-6420`: on message submission the permission profile is set to `None` specifically when the sandbox policy is the (legacy) `SandboxPolicy::ExternalSandbox` variant, and otherwise the profile from session config is passed through.
